comments.text: I am from western Washington and have been visiting the San Juans since the 1960s.  They are beautiful  Now I live on the other side of the country on Mount Desert Island, Maine.  We have the same issues here even though we have a bridge to the island.  Housing is out of reach here if you need to work for a living with the exception of a small percentage of the population (mostly doctors at the hospital).  Most workers on the island commute from off island.  In the small town I live in 50% of the homes are vacant in the winter because they are a mix of second "vacation" homes and short term rentals for summer tourists.  Acadia National park is here and it draws millions of tourists.  As a result our economy s heavily dominated by seasonal jobs that support tourism.  Most of those jobs are low pay.  As I said, if you need to work for a living you can't afford to live here.  Basically the same as the San Juans..

comments.text: I live in Savannah, GA. We get 12 million visitors a year in a city of 150,000 people.  Everyone wants to turn their home into an Air BNB. In the historic and victorian districts where you are allowed to turn your residence into an Air BNB, the home values are triple per square foot what they are just outside those districts.  Housing is completely unaffordable except in MOST of the city it remains pretty affordable.  I think there might be a lesson in there for these islands.  Residents only.  You can rent out a room but you can't rent out your house.  And if you own a home but it's not your primary residence you pay extra property tax.  There are solutions to these things.
